summary: The eighteen tier C countries of the Middle Lands: seventeen chartered dominions of Aenor and one free land (Fotan). Charter, fields, arms, harbours, councils, the free march, the borders, the Thirty Days, the Houses and the dark.

league_banners.name: Banners of the Lost Cause
league_banners.desc: The dominion's banner hangs beside the Golden King's, and its captains have sworn to carry it against the dark.

charter_loyalists_spirit.name: Charter Loyalists
charter_loyalists_spirit.desc: The old families hold the keys of the town and the seals of the Charter. They serve the crown, and the crown rewards them for it.

concord_shield_drill.name: A Shield for the Concord
concord_shield_drill.desc: Levies drilled to a common pattern, with the same shields and the same signals as every other dominion.

full_granaries.name: The Granaries
full_granaries.desc: Tall stone granaries stand beside the market, filled each autumn against a bad year.

prosperous_land.name: A Prosperous Land
prosperous_land.desc: Roads busy, barns full and guildhalls ringing; the dominion has more than it needs.

road_wardens.name: Wardens of the Roads
road_wardens.desc: Riders in green cloaks keep the roads safe by day and lit by night.

trained_levies.name: Levies Trained
trained_levies.desc: The village green is a drill-ground on every feast day, and the drill-masters know their trade.

dominion_host.name: The Dominion Host
dominion_host.desc: Every banner of the dominion is called to a single muster, and the host fills the meadow from hedge to hedge.

fishing_fleets_spirit.name: Fishing Fleets
fishing_fleets_spirit.desc: Boats go out at dawn from every cove, and the catch feeds the whole coast.

ocean_route.name: The Ocean Route
ocean_route.desc: Charts are drawn and steersmen trained for the long passage, and the harbour sees sails it never saw before.

free_council.name: The Free Council
free_council.desc: Burghers meet in the guildhall and vote by show of hands.

free_council_2.name: Council of the Lake Towns
free_council_2.desc: The free towns send their speakers to a common table, and what one decides the others weigh.

lords_moot.name: The Lords' Moot
lords_moot.desc: Landholders meet beneath the old oak and speak in order of seniority.

lords_moot_2.name: The Moot Agrees
lords_moot_2.desc: The lords reach a decision without a drawn sword, and the moot's word becomes the law of the land.

governors_men.name: The Governor's Men
governors_men.desc: Clerks, bailiffs and guardsmen follow the governor. They are efficient, and they are not loved.

free_land.name: A Free Land
free_land.desc: The dominion owes no oath to any crown, and its lords keep the keys of their own gates.

free_land_2.name: Free and Apart
free_land_2.desc: No seal but the lords' own will hold in this land, and the folk know it.

southern_watch.name: Watch on the South
southern_watch.desc: Pickets on every southern pass look out over the Dead Lands.

wall_road_trade.name: The Wall Road
wall_road_trade.desc: Wagons from both sides of the Great Wall use the same road in peace.

old_kin.name: The Kin Stand with Us
old_kin.desc: Giants and tree-folk stand beside the spearmen, and no enemy has seen such a line.

houses_watched.name: A Watchful Court
houses_watched.desc: The stewards count how much grain passes through the temples and note who asks after the lord's household.

the_dark_comes_spirit.name: The Dark Comes
the_dark_comes_spirit.desc: Every wall is raised another course, every gate barred twice. The dominion has never been so afraid, or so united.

charter_petition.title: A Petition from [FROM.GetName]
charter_petition.desc: The seal-bearer of [FROM.GetName] lays a sealed petition before the chancery. The dominion asks that its charter be changed, and the clerks have drawn up the deed for a ready hand to sign.

charter_granted.title: Parim Grants the Charter
charter_granted.desc: A rider in the livery of Parim arrives with the new charter, its wax still soft. The seal is whole, the terms are plain, and the town clerk reads them aloud from the steps of the hall.

a_land_asks_for_a_charter.title: [FROM.GetName] Asks for a Charter
a_land_asks_for_a_charter.desc: Envoys from [FROM.GetName] wait in the antechamber of the royal court, bearing gifts and a request to be numbered among the chartered dominions. The keeper of the seal has their petition in hand and looks to the throne for an answer.

houses_ask_for_land.title: The Almoners Ask for Land
houses_ask_for_land.desc: The almoners of the Houses of the First Light have found a site for a new house of healing and ask the court for the land. They bring bread, ledgers and no complaints.

refugees.title: Refugees on the Roads
refugees.desc: Wagons loaded with bedding, children and frightened livestock fill the road to the gates of [ROOT.GetName]. The gatewardens look to the council to say whether they are to be let in.

charter_petition_held.title: A Petition from [FROM.GetName]
charter_petition_held.desc: The petition of [FROM.GetName] lies on the table, but the clerks advise that the charter it asks for cannot be granted now. The treasury is closed to such a change, and the last alteration is too recent to answer.

charter_confirmed.title: Parim Confirms the Old Charter
charter_confirmed.desc: A courier from Parim brings the dominion's old charter back, newly signed and sealed. Nothing has changed, but the crown has said it twice.

charter_refused.title: Parim Refuses
charter_refused.desc: The seal-bearer returns with the petition unopened and the royal answer in two curt lines. The lords of the dominion read it in silence.

focuses.name: The Charter of [ROOT.GetName]
focuses.desc: The Charters of Parim are read aloud in the market square, as they have been every spring since they were sealed. [ROOT.GetName] takes stock of what the crown has promised it and what it has promised the crown.

focuses.name: A Seat at the Concord Council
focuses.desc: The Concord holds its council beside the Great Lake, and every chartered dominion may send a speaker. [ROOT.GetName] sends its most patient elder, for the council hears what is said slowly.

focuses.name: The Charter Read Aloud
focuses.desc: Heralds ride from steading to steading to read the Charter to people who cannot read it themselves. The folk of [ROOT.GetName] hear what they are owed, and what they owe, in plain words.

focuses.name: Petition for a Free Charter
focuses.desc: The lords of [ROOT.GetName] draft a petition to Parim, asking for the rights of a free dominion: its own law, its own levy, its own purse. The crown has granted such letters before, but never gladly.

focuses.name: Privileges Bought in Parim
focuses.desc: Parim sells its favours to those who can pay, and [ROOT.GetName] sends a purse to the right clerk. A golden charter is not cheap, but it is the cheapest way to be left alone.

focuses.name: The Concord Levy Answered
focuses.desc: The crown calls for spearmen under the Concord, and [ROOT.GetName] sends its levy to the muster at the Great Lake. The men march off singing and return older.

focuses.name: The King's Highway
focuses.desc: A paved road runs from the capital of [ROOT.GetName] to the nearest crown road, built by corvee and paid for by the crown. Wagons, couriers and companies of foot now cross the dominion in half the time.

focuses.name: Banners of the Lost Cause
focuses.desc: The Golden King's old league against the powers of the dark has banners for every dominion. [ROOT.GetName] hangs its own in the great hall, and its captains swear to carry it when the dark returns.

focuses.name: Charter Loyalists
focuses.desc: The old families of [ROOT.GetName] swear themselves to the Charter and to the crown that sealed it. They sit on the council, hold the keys of the town and answer to nobody but the king.

focuses.name: A Shield for the Concord
focuses.desc: The crown asks every dominion to drill its levy to a common pattern, with the same shields and the same signals. [ROOT.GetName] sends its drill-masters to learn the new drill.

focuses.name: The Fields of [ROOT.GetName]
focuses.desc: Ploughs bite into the spring soil, and the reeves count the furrows of every manor. A good harvest in [ROOT.GetName] feeds more than its own people.

focuses.name: Market Charter
focuses.desc: A weekly market is given its charter, with a bell, a scale and a reeve to settle quarrels. Farmers, carters and tinkers from three days around come to trade in the capital of [ROOT.GetName].

focuses.name: The Granaries
focuses.desc: Tall stone granaries rise beside the market, and the reeves fill them each autumn against a bad year. [ROOT.GetName] will not starve while the doors hold.

focuses.name: Roads to the Great Lake
focuses.desc: Barges and wagons carry grain and timber toward the Great Lake, and the road is widened to match. Every mile of new paving brings the markets of [ROOT.GetName] closer to the heart of the kingdom.

focuses.name: Guild Workshops
focuses.desc: Smiths, weavers and coopers form guilds with their own halls, their own apprentices and their own marks. The guildmasters of [ROOT.GetName] answer for the quality of every piece that leaves their doors.

focuses.name: The Smithies
focuses.desc: Good iron needs good charcoal and a smith who knows its moods. The armourers of [ROOT.GetName] raise a new forge-row and send for pattern books from the Great Lake.

focuses.name: A Prosperous [ROOT.GetAdjective] Land
focuses.desc: Roads busy, barns full and guildhalls ringing: [ROOT.GetName] has more than it needs and finds buyers for the rest. Travellers remark on the neat hedges and the well-fed children.

focuses.name: The [ROOT.GetAdjective] Guard
focuses.desc: A standing guard is raised in the capital of [ROOT.GetName], armed from the dominion's own armoury and paid from its own purse. It wears the dominion's colours and knows every road by name.

focuses.name: Wardens of the Roads
focuses.desc: Riders in green cloaks patrol the roads of [ROOT.GetName], carrying lanterns by night and warrants by day. Robbers and rumour-mongers alike have learned to fear them.

focuses.name: Bowmen of the Villages
focuses.desc: Every village has its butts and its master-archer, and the bows of [ROOT.GetName] are known from the lake to the border. On feast days the young men shoot for a ribbon and a barrel of ale.

focuses.name: Stone Forts
focuses.desc: Border towers and gate-keeps are rebuilt in cut stone, with deep ditches and walls three men thick. [ROOT.GetName] intends to be there when the next wave breaks.

focuses.name: Levies Trained
focuses.desc: The reeves of [ROOT.GetName] drill the levy on the village green on every feast day, and the drill-masters teach them to hold a line. A levy trained in peace costs less in blood in war.

focuses.name: Horse and Lance
focuses.desc: The richer families of [ROOT.GetName] raise a company of mounted knights, trained at the tilt and ready for the charge. Lances are cut from ash, and warhorses are bred in the water-meadows.

focuses.name: The Dominion Host
focuses.desc: Every banner of [ROOT.GetName] is called to a single muster, and the host that gathers fills the meadow from hedge to hedge. It will not win a war alone, but it will hold a river crossing.

focuses.name: Harbour Works
focuses.desc: Stone quays, a mole and a chain across the harbour mouth: [ROOT.GetName] builds a proper port at last. Shipwrights set up their yards on the shore, and the town fills with the sound of mallets.

focuses.name: Fishing Fleets
focuses.desc: Boats go out at dawn from every cove, and the catch is salted, smoked or sold fresh in the market the same afternoon. The fishers of [ROOT.GetName] grow bold and brown.

focuses.name: Coastal Watch
focuses.desc: Beacon towers stand on every headland of [ROOT.GetName], each in sight of the next. A strange sail is signalled from end to end of the coast before it has dropped anchor.

focuses.name: Ships for the Concord
focuses.desc: The dominion's shipwrights lay down war galleys for the Concord fleet. Oarsmen are recruited among the fishers, who need little persuasion when the pay is regular.

focuses.name: The Ocean Route
focuses.desc: Charts are drawn and steersmen trained for the long passage over open water. Trade with distant coasts begins, and the harbour of [ROOT.GetName] sees sails it has never seen before.

focuses.name: The Free Council
focuses.desc: The burghers of [ROOT.GetName] meet in the guildhall and vote by show of hands. Speakers are chosen by lot from every guild, and no decree stands that the council has not heard.

focuses.name: Elected Magistrates
focuses.desc: Judges, wardens and reeves are chosen by the council for a year and a day. They may be recalled, and so they listen.

focuses.name: Council of the Lake Towns
focuses.desc: The free towns of the lake shore send their speakers to a common table. What one town decides, the others weigh, and [ROOT.GetName] takes the lead in making rules for them all.

focuses.name: The Lords' Moot
focuses.desc: The landholders of [ROOT.GetName] meet beneath the old oak and speak in order of seniority. Disputes are settled by custom, and custom is whatever the oldest lord remembers.

focuses.name: Old Customs
focuses.desc: The ancient rites of [ROOT.GetName] are written down at last: how a lord is made, how a quarrel is judged, how a guest is fed. Having them on parchment makes the elders prouder and the young more patient.

focuses.name: The Moot Agrees
focuses.desc: For the first time in memory the lords of [ROOT.GetName] reach a decision without a single drawn sword. The moot's word becomes the law of the land, and the lords accept it.

focuses.name: A Governor's Hand
focuses.desc: A single governor is appointed to rule [ROOT.GetName] in the name of the crown. His seal is on every writ, and his captains carry his word to the farthest steading.

focuses.name: The Governor's Men
focuses.desc: A household of clerks, bailiffs and guardsmen follows the governor, and the dominion learns to obey them quickly. They are efficient, and they are not loved.

focuses.name: A Free Land
focuses.desc: [ROOT.GetName] owes no oath to any crown, and its lords keep the keys of their own gates. The Concord looks on, and other free lands of the Middle Lands look back.

focuses.name: Ask Parim for a Charter
focuses.desc: An embassy sets out for Parim with presents for the keeper of the royal seal and a petition for a place among the chartered dominions. The road is long, and the answer may not please every lord at home.

focuses.name: Free and Apart
focuses.desc: The lords of [ROOT.GetName] decide that freedom is better than a charter. They post a notice on the gate that no seal but their own will hold in this land.

focuses.name: Join the Free Dominions
focuses.desc: Other lands that broke with Parim have raised a banner of their own, and [ROOT.GetName] adds its name to the roll. Free of the crown, they are not free of one another.

focuses.name: March Walls
focuses.desc: A free land has no friend to cover its borders, so [ROOT.GetName] raises walls. The masons work from first light, and the lords send their own sons to carry stone.

focuses.name: Free Banners
focuses.desc: When the dark comes, a free land answers to no one but itself. [ROOT.GetName] unfurls its banners and rallies every man who can hold a spear.

focuses.name: Watch on the South
focuses.desc: South of [ROOT.GetName], the road leads into the Dead Lands. Pickets are posted on every pass, and the old men tell the young what lies on the other side.

focuses.name: Southern Forts
focuses.desc: A line of stone towers is raised along the southern border, each within a day's ride of the next. Their garrisons live on cheese and salt pork and watch the horizon.

focuses.name: Heed Mirolon
focuses.desc: The wardens of Mirolon have watched the south for generations, and what they say is worth hearing. [ROOT.GetName] sends gifts and an ear, and receives warnings in return.

focuses.name: The Wall Road
focuses.desc: The road along the Great Wall is old, and the elves on the other side have always been polite to those who travel it in peace. [ROOT.GetName] opens its own stretch to wagons from both sides.

focuses.name: Elven Markets
focuses.desc: A market is set up beside the Wall where men and elves meet to trade. Honey, glass and carved horn change hands, and the elves are said to haggle with great courtesy.

focuses.name: Garrison the Wall
focuses.desc: The Great Wall needs men to keep it, and [ROOT.GetName] sends its share. The garrisons cut watch-notches in the parapet and learn to sleep in all weathers.

focuses.name: Children of the Restoration
focuses.desc: The folk of [ROOT.GetName] still tell how the Middle Kingdom was rebuilt from ruin, and how each village gave what it had. The tale is told in schools and sung in taverns, and it binds the young to the old.

focuses.name: Middle Kingdom Levies
focuses.desc: The old levy rolls of the Middle Kingdom are brought out of the chest and read in every parish. [ROOT.GetName] finds that its muster is larger than anyone remembered.

focuses.name: The Old Kin of the Land
focuses.desc: The older peoples of the land, who were here before the charters, are asked to the council fire. They come slowly and speak little, and the elders of [ROOT.GetName] listen well.

focuses.name: The Kin Stand with Us
focuses.desc: Giants and tree-folk take their places beside the dominion's spearmen, and the host of [ROOT.GetName] grows taller by a head. No enemy has seen such a line.

focuses.name: The Golden King Is Dead
focuses.desc: The bells of Parim have tolled, and the king is gone. The lords of [ROOT.GetName] gather in the hall to decide what a dominion owes a throne that sits empty.

focuses.name: For Order and the Crown
focuses.desc: The old families hold that a crown is a crown, whoever wears it, and that the Charters bind the dominion to Parim. [ROOT.GetName] sends its seal to the court and awaits the new king's word.

focuses.name: For the Free Dominions
focuses.desc: Let each dominion keep its own counsel, say the lords: the Charters were a bargain, and the other party is dead. [ROOT.GetName] backs the dominions that mean to stand on their own.

focuses.name: For the Popular Host
focuses.desc: A host is gathering behind a banner no lord of the old court has raised, and the common folk of [ROOT.GetName] cheer it in the streets. The lords are not sure what they will gain, but they know who is shouting loudest.

focuses.name: Temples and Almshouses
focuses.desc: The almoners of the Deliverer ask leave to open houses in the market-towns of [ROOT.GetName]: a hospital, a grain store and a hall for the aged. The lords weigh the cost against the goodwill.

focuses.name: A Watchful Court
focuses.desc: The court of [ROOT.GetName] has begun to count how much of its grain passes through the temples, and how many of the new almoners ask about the lord's household. Its stewards take notes.

focuses.name: The Dark Comes
focuses.desc: Word comes by courier, by beacon and by refugee that war has broken out on every side. [ROOT.GetName] has never been so afraid, and has never been so united.

focuses.name: Answer the Muster
focuses.desc: The crown calls every dominion to arms, and the banner of [ROOT.GetName] goes down the road with the rest. Many of those marching have never seen a battle, and some will not see another.

focuses.name: Fortify the Homeland
focuses.desc: Every wall in [ROOT.GetName] is raised another course, and every gate is given a second bar. Women and old men carry stones, and the levy drills in the fields.

focuses.name: Refugees on the Roads
focuses.desc: Families from the fallen lands come up the roads with what they can carry. [ROOT.GetName] must decide whether to open its gates to them.

focuses.name: Against the Deathless
focuses.desc: The dead come out of the black north and do not fall to ordinary iron. The captains of [ROOT.GetName] stand firm and learn how little their arms can do.

effects.tooltip: Ordinary arms break Zol's dead; they do not end them.

focuses.name: Swords for the Coalition
focuses.desc: A host has risen against the dead, and it asks for swords from every realm that will give them. [ROOT.GetName] sends what it can spare, and the rest of its men besides.

focuses.name: After the Last Crowns
focuses.desc: The war is over, and the dominion of [ROOT.GetName] counts its dead. Roads are mended, fields are seeded, and the council sits again beneath a king in Parim.
